paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the closer you get to the holy King, the more you see how much you need Him. Isaiah sees the Lord on His throne, hears the seraphim cry "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts," and what comes out of his mouth is "Woe is me, for I am ruined." (Isaiah 6:3, 5) I felt that. An important guest walks in and suddenly I see EVERY crumb on my apron. Being honest about that isn't the end of the story, it's the doorway.

Because look what happens next. The seraph touches Isaiah's lips with the coal and says, "Your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned for." (Isaiah 6:7) Isaiah didn't clean himself up first. He didn't bake his way into the room. The Lord dealt with the sin, and then Isaiah heard the question, "Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?" and answered, "Here am I. Send me!" (Isaiah 6:8) Forgiven people say yes, friend, and they say it with open hands.

Now, the message Isaiah is sent with is a heavy one, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. (Isaiah 6:9-12) But the passage ends with a stump: "the holy seed will be a stump in the land." (Isaiah 6:13) Cut down, but still in the ground. So if you're wearing thin today, remember that the God who is holy, who forgives, and who sends is the same God who keeps something STILL THERE. I'm living proof, baker, and I've got the gold base to show for it.
